sanskrit: kurukṣetrasya tad dvāraṃ viśrutaṃ bharatarṣabha pradakṣiṇam upāvṛtya tīrthasevī samāhitaḥ
english: That renowned gateway of Kurukṣetra, O bull among Bhāratas — the pilgrim, collected in mind, having circumambulated it clockwise,

sanskrit: saṃmite puṣkarāṇāṃ ca snātvārcya pitṛdevatāḥ jāmadagnyena rāmeṇa āhṛte vai mahātmanā kṛtakṛtyo bhaved rājann aśvamedhaṃ ca vindati
english: having bathed at the measure of Puṣkara and having worshipped the ancestors and the gods — that which was brought by the great-souled Rāma, son of Jamadagni — O king, such a person becomes fulfilled and obtains the fruit of the Aśvamedha sacrifice.

sanskrit: tato rāmahradān gacchet tīrthasevī narādhipa yatra rāmeṇa rājendra tarasā dīptatejasā kṣatram utsādya vīryeṇa hradāḥ pañca niveśitāḥ
english: Then the tirtha-pilgrim should go to the lakes of Rāma, O lord of men; where Rāma, O king of kings, with his blazing splendour and swiftness, having extirpated the kshatriya class by his valour, established five lakes.

sanskrit: pūrayitvā naravyāghra rudhireṇeti naḥ śrutam pitaras tarpitāḥ sarve tathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ tatas te pitaraḥ prītā rāmam ūcur mahīpate
english: Having filled them with blood — thus we have heard — all the fathers were gratified, and likewise the grandfathers. Then those pleased fathers spoke to Rāma, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: rāma rāma mahābhāga prītāḥ sma tava bhārgava anayā pitṛbhaktyā ca vikrameṇa ca te vibho varaṃ vṛṇīṣva bhadraṃ te kim icchasi mahādyute
english: "Rāma, Rāma, O greatly fortunate one, O Bhārgava, we are pleased with you — by this devotion to ancestors and by your valour, O lord. Choose a boon, may you prosper; what do you desire, O greatly resplendent one?"

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa rājendra rāmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ abravīt prāñjalir vākyaṃ pitṝn sa gagane sthitān
english: Thus addressed, O king of kings, Rāma, the foremost of warriors, spoke words with folded hands to the fathers standing in the sky:

sanskrit: bhavanto yadi me prītā yady anugrāhyatā mayi pitṛprasādād iccheyaṃ tapasāpyāyanaṃ punaḥ
english: "If you are pleased with me, if I am worthy of your grace, then by the favour of the ancestors I wish for increase of my austerities again.

sanskrit: yac ca roṣābhibhūtena kṣatram utsāditaṃ mayā tataś ca pāpān mucyeyaṃ yuṣmākaṃ tejasā hy aham hradāś ca tīrthabhūtā me bhaveyur bhuvi viśrutāḥ
english: And from the sin by which, overcome with wrath, I exterminated the kshatriya class — may I be freed from that sin by your splendour; and may these lakes become sacred tirthas renowned on earth."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā śubhaṃ vākyaṃ rāmasya pitaras tadā pratyūcuḥ paramaprītā rāmaṃ harṣasamanvitāḥ
english: Having heard these auspicious words of Rāma, the fathers then replied to Rāma, supremely delighted and filled with joy:

sanskrit: tapas te vardhatāṃ bhūyaḥ pitṛbhaktyā viśeṣataḥ yac ca roṣābhibhūtena kṣatram utsāditaṃ tvayā
english: "May your austerities increase further, especially through your devotion to the ancestors; and as for what was done by you in anger — the extermination of the kshatriyas —

sanskrit: tataś ca pāpān muktas tvaṃ karmabhis te ca pātitāḥ hradāś ca tava tīrthatvaṃ gamiṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ
english: from that sin you are freed, and those brought low by your deeds — and these lakes shall undoubtedly attain the status of sacred tirthas."

sanskrit: hradeṣv eteṣu yaḥ snātvā pitṝn saṃtarpayiṣyati pitaras tasya vai prītā dāsyanti bhuvi durlabham īpsitaṃ manasaḥ kāmaṃ svargalokaṃ ca śāśvatam
english: Whoever, having bathed in these lakes, will gratify his ancestors — the fathers, well-pleased with him, will grant what is difficult to obtain on earth: the desired wish of his heart and the eternal heavenly world.

sanskrit: evaṃ dattvā varān rājan rāmasya pitaras tadā āmantrya bhārgavaṃ prītās tatraivāntardadhus tadā
english: Having thus bestowed the boons upon Rāma, O king, the fathers then, taking leave of the Bhārgava, pleased, vanished on the spot.

sanskrit: evaṃ rāmahradāḥ puṇyā bhārgavasya mahātmanaḥ snātvā hradeṣu rāmasya brahmacārī śubhavrataḥ rāmam abhyarcya rājendra labhed bahu suvarṇakam
english: Thus the lakes of Rāma are holy, belonging to the great-souled Bhārgava. A celibate of pure vow, having bathed in the lakes of Rāma and having worshipped Rāma, O king of kings, would obtain much gold.

sanskrit: vaṃśamūlakam āsādya tīrthasevī kurūdvaha svavaṃśam uddhared rājan snātvā vai vaṃśamūlake
english: Reaching Vamshamulaka, O foremost of the Kurus, the tirtha-pilgrim, having bathed at Vamshamulaka, would lift up his own lineage, O king.

sanskrit: kāyaśodhanam āsādya tīrthaṃ bharatasattama śarīraśuddhiḥ snātasya tasmiṃs tīrthe na saṃśayaḥ śuddhadehaś ca saṃyāti śubhāṃl lokān anuttamān
english: Reaching the tirtha called Kayashodhana, O best of Bhāratas, the body of one who has bathed at that tirtha is without doubt purified; and with a purified body he goes to the excellent, unsurpassable worlds.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam lokā yatroddhṛtāḥ pūrvaṃ viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā
english: Then one should go, O king of kings, to the tirtha renowned in all three worlds, where the worlds were formerly lifted up by Viṣṇu the mighty.

sanskrit: lokoddhāraṃ samāsādya tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam snātvā tīrthavare rājaṃl lokān uddharate svakān śrītīrthaṃ ca samāsādya vindate śriyam uttamām
english: Reaching Lokoddhara, the tirtha renowned in all three worlds, having bathed at that best of tirthas, O king, one lifts up one's own kindred; and reaching Shritirtha, one obtains the highest prosperity.

sanskrit: kapilātīrtham āsādya brahmacārī samāhitaḥ tatra snātvārcayitvā ca daivatāni pitṝṃs tathā kapilānāṃ sahasrasya phalaṃ vindati mānavaḥ
english: Reaching the tirtha of Kapila, a celibate with collected mind, having bathed there and having worshipped the gods and ancestors, a man obtains the fruit of a thousand kapila cows.

sanskrit: sūryatīrthaṃ samāsādya snātvā niyatamānasaḥ arcayitvā pitṝn devān upavāsaparāyaṇaḥ agniṣṭomam avāpnoti sūryalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Reaching the tirtha of the Sun, having bathed with a disciplined mind, having worshipped the ancestors and the gods, devoted to fasting, one obtains the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice and goes to the world of the Sun.

sanskrit: gavāṃbhavanam āsādya tīrthasevī yathākramam tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvāṇo gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: Reaching Gavambhavana, the tirtha-pilgrim, performing the ritual bath there in proper order, would obtain the fruit of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: śaṅkhinīṃ tatra āsādya tīrthasevī kurūdvaha devyās tīrthe naraḥ snātvā labhate rūpam uttamam
english: Reaching Shankhini there, O foremost of the Kurus, a man having bathed at the tirtha of the goddess obtains excellent beauty.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra dvārapālam arantukam tasya tīrthaṃ sarasvatyāṃ yakṣendrasya mahātmanaḥ tatra snātvā naro rājann agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
english: Then one should go, O king of kings, to the gatekeeper Arantuka — the tirtha of that great-souled king of yakshas on the Sarasvatī; having bathed there, O king, a man would obtain the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña brahmāvartaṃ narādhipa brahmāvarte naraḥ snātvā brahmalokam avāpnuyāt
english: Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to Brahmāvarta, O lord of men; a man having bathed at Brahmāvarta would attain the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta dharmajña sutīrthakam anuttamam yatra saṃnihitā nityaṃ pitaro daivataiḥ saha
english: Then one should go, O knower of dharma, to the unsurpassable Sutirthaka, where the ancestors are always present together with the gods.

sanskrit: tatrābhiṣekaṃ kurvīta pitṛdevārcane rataḥ aśvamedham avāpnoti pitṛlokaṃ ca gacchati
english: There one devoted to the worship of ancestors and gods should perform the ritual bath; one obtains the Aśvamedha sacrifice and goes to the world of the ancestors.

sanskrit: tato 'mbuvaśyaṃ dharmajña samāsādya yathākramam kośeśvarasya tīrtheṣu snātvā bharatasattama sarvavyādhivinirmukto brahmaloke mahīyate
english: Then, O knower of dharma, reaching Ambuvasya in proper order, and bathing at the tirthas of Kosheshvara, O best of Bhāratas, one is freed from all diseases and is honoured in the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: mātṛtīrthaṃ ca tatraiva yatra snātasya bhārata prajā vivardhate rājann anantāṃ cāśnute śriyam
english: And Matritirtha is there likewise, where, O Bhārata, for one who has bathed, O king, his progeny multiplies and he enjoys boundless prosperity.

sanskrit: tataḥ śītavanaṃ gacchen niyato niyatāśanaḥ tīrthaṃ tatra mahārāja mahad anyatra durlabham
english: Then one should go to Shitavana, disciplined and with regulated diet; the tirtha there, O great king, is great and difficult to find elsewhere.

sanskrit: punāti darśanād eva daṇḍenaikaṃ narādhipa keśān abhyukṣya vai tasmin pūto bhavati bhārata
english: It purifies even one guilty of using a stick merely by seeing it, O lord of men; and having sprinkled one's hair at that place, one becomes purified, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tīrthaṃ tatra mahārāja śvānalomāpahaṃ smṛtam yatra viprā naravyāghra vidvāṃsas tīrthatatparāḥ
english: That tirtha there, O great king, is known as the remover of dog's hair; where, O tiger among men, learned brahmins devoted to tirthas —

sanskrit: śvānalomāpanayane tīrthe bharatasattama prāṇāyāmair nirharanti śvalomāni dvijottamāḥ
english: — at this tirtha for the removal of dog's hair, O best of Bhāratas, the best of twice-born remove dog's hair through pranayama practices.

sanskrit: pūtātmānaś ca rājendra prayānti paramāṃ gatim daśāśvamedhikaṃ caiva tasmiṃs tīrthe mahīpate tatra snātvā naravyāghra gaccheta paramāṃ gatim
english: With purified souls, O king of kings, they proceed to the highest state; and the Dashasvamedha fruit too — at that tirtha, O lord of the earth, having bathed there, O tiger among men, one proceeds to the highest state.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra mānuṣaṃ lokaviśrutam yatra kṛṣṇamṛgā rājan vyādhena paripīḍitāḥ avagāhya tasmin sarasi mānuṣatvam upāgatāḥ
english: Then one should go, O king of kings, to Manusham, renowned in the world; where, O king, black deer tormented by a hunter, having plunged into that lake, attained human form.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tīrthe naraḥ snātvā brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā svargaloke mahīyate
english: A man having bathed at that tirtha, a celibate with conquered senses, with a soul purified of all sins, is honoured in the heavenly world.

sanskrit: mānuṣasya tu pūrveṇa krośamātre mahīpate āpagā nāma vikhyātā nadī siddhaniṣevitā
english: To the east of Manusham, at the distance of a krosa, O lord of the earth, is the famous river called Apaga, frequented by the siddhas.

sanskrit: śyāmākabhojanaṃ tatra yaḥ prayacchati mānavaḥ devān pitṝṃś ca uddiśya tasya dharmaphalaṃ mahat ekasmin bhojite vipre koṭir bhavati bhojitā
english: Whatever man offers a meal of shyamaka grain there, dedicating it to the gods and ancestors — his religious merit is great; when one brahmin is fed, a crore of brahmins count as fed.

sanskrit: tatra snātvārcayitvā ca daivatāni pitṝṃs tathā uṣitvā rajanīm ekām agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
english: Having bathed there and having worshipped the gods and ancestors, and having stayed one night, one would obtain the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra brahmaṇaḥ sthānam uttamam brahmodumbaram ity eva prakāśaṃ bhuvi bhārata
english: Then one should go, O king of kings, to the supreme abode of Brahmā, known on earth as Brahmodumbara, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tatra saptarṣikuṇḍeṣu snātasya kurupuṃgava kedāre caiva rājendra kapiṣṭhalamahātmanaḥ
english: There, for one who has bathed in the pools of the seven sages, O bull among Kurus, and also at Kedara, O king of kings, through the greatness of Kapishtala —

sanskrit: brahmāṇam abhigamyātha śuciḥ prayatamānasaḥ sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā brahmalokaṃ prapadyate
english: — having approached Brahmā, pure and with controlled mind, one with a soul purified of all sins attains the world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: kapiṣṭhalasya kedāraṃ samāsādya sudurlabham antardhānam avāpnoti tapasā dagdhakilbiṣaḥ
english: Reaching the Kedara of Kapishtala, which is very difficult to reach, one whose sin is burned away by austerity obtains invisibility.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra sarakaṃ lokaviśrutam kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśyām abhigamya vṛṣadhvajam labhate sarvakāmān hi svargalokaṃ ca gacchati
english: Then one should go, O king of kings, to Saraka, renowned in the world; approaching Vṛṣadhvaja on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, one obtains all desires and goes to the heavenly world.

sanskrit: tisraḥ koṭyas tu tīrthānāṃ sarake kurunandana rudrakoṭis tathā kūpe hradeṣu ca mahīpate ilāspadaṃ ca tatraiva tīrthaṃ bharatasattama
english: Thirty million tirthas are in Saraka, O joy of the Kurus; Rudrakoti also at the well, and in the lakes, O lord of the earth; and Ilaspada too is there as a tirtha, O best of Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tatra snātvārcayitvā ca pitṝn devāṃś ca bhārata na durgatim avāpnoti vājapeyaṃ ca vindati
english: Having bathed there and having worshipped the ancestors and gods, O Bhārata, one does not come to ill fate and obtains the Vājapeya sacrifice.

sanskrit: kiṃdāne ca naraḥ snātvā kiṃjapye ca mahīpate aprameyam avāpnoti dānaṃ japyaṃ ca bhārata
english: A man having bathed at Kimdana and at Kimjapya, O lord of the earth, obtains immeasurable fruit of gift-giving and of recitation, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kalaśyāṃ cāpy upaspṛśya śraddadhāno jitendriyaḥ agniṣṭomasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: And touching the waters at Kalashya, a man who is faithful and has conquered his senses obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.

sanskrit: sarakasya tu pūrveṇa nāradasya mahātmanaḥ tīrthaṃ kuruvaraśreṣṭha anājanmeti viśrutam
english: To the east of Saraka is the tirtha of the great-souled Nārada, O foremost of the best of Kurus, known as Anajanma.

sanskrit: tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā prāṇāṃś cotsṛjya bhārata nāradenābhyanujñāto lokān prāpnoti durlabhān
english: A man having bathed at that tirtha and having given up his life, O Bhārata, with the permission of Nārada, attains worlds difficult to reach.

sanskrit: śuklapakṣe daśamyāṃ tu puṇḍarīkaṃ samāviśet tatra snātvā naro rājan puṇḍarīkaphalaṃ labhet
english: On the tenth day of the bright fortnight one should enter Pundarika; a man having bathed there, O king, would obtain the fruit of the Pundarika sacrifice.

sanskrit: tatas triviṣṭapaṃ gacchet triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam tatra vaitaraṇī puṇyā nadī pāpapramocanī
english: Then one should go to Trivishthapa, renowned in all three worlds; there is the holy river Vaitaraṇī, the remover of sins.

sanskrit: tatra snātvārcayitvā ca śūlapāṇiṃ vṛṣadhvajam sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā gaccheta paramāṃ gatim
english: Having bathed there and having worshipped Shulapani, the bearer of the bull-banner, with a soul purified of all sins, one would proceed to the highest state.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra phalakīvanam uttamam yatra devāḥ sadā rājan phalakīvanam āśritāḥ tapaś caranti vipulaṃ bahuvarṣasahasrakam
english: Then one should go, O king of kings, to the excellent Phalakirvana; where the gods, O king, ever resorting to Phalakirvana, perform great austerities for many thousands of years.

sanskrit: dṛṣadvatyāṃ naraḥ snātvā tarpayitvā ca devatāḥ agniṣṭomātirātrābhyāṃ phalaṃ vindati bhārata
english: A man having bathed in the Drishadavati and having gratified the gods obtains the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma and the Atirātra, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tīrthe ca sarvadevānāṃ snātvā bharatasattama gosahasrasya rājendra phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
english: And having bathed at the tirtha of all the gods, O best of Bhāratas, a man, O king of kings, obtains the fruit of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: pāṇikhāte naraḥ snātvā tarpayitvā ca devatāḥ rājasūyam avāpnoti ṛṣilokaṃ ca gacchati
english: A man having bathed at Panikhata and having gratified the gods obtains the Rājasūya sacrifice and goes to the world of the sages.

sanskrit: tato gaccheta rājendra miśrakaṃ tīrtham uttamam tatra tīrthāni rājendra miśritāni mahātmanā
english: Then one should go, O king of kings, to the excellent tirtha of Mishraka; there the tirthas have been mixed together, O king of kings, by the great soul —

sanskrit: vyāsena nṛpaśārdūla dvijārtham iti naḥ śrutam sarvatīrtheṣu sa snāti miśrake snāti yo naraḥ
english: — by Vyāsa for the sake of the twice-born, thus we have heard, O tiger among kings; whoever bathes at Mishraka, he bathes in all the tirthas.

sanskrit: tato vyāsavanaṃ gacchen niyato niyatāśanaḥ manojave naraḥ snātvā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: Then one should go to the forest of Vyāsa, disciplined and with regulated diet; a man having bathed in Manojava would obtain the fruit of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: gatvā madhuvaṭīṃ cāpi devyās tīrthaṃ naraḥ śuciḥ tatra snātvārcayed devān pitṝṃś ca prayataḥ śuciḥ sa devyā samanujñāto gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: And going to Madhuvati, the tirtha of the goddess, a man who is pure, having bathed there and worshipped the gods and ancestors with controlled mind and purity, with the permission of the goddess, would obtain the fruit of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: kauśikyāḥ saṃgame yas tu dṛṣadvatyāś ca bhārata snāti vai niyatāhāraḥ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: Whoever, at the confluence of the Kauśikī and the Drishadavati, O Bhārata, bathes with regulated diet, is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: tato vyāsasthalī nāma yatra vyāsena dhīmatā putraśokābhitaptena dehatyāgārthaniścayaḥ
english: Then there is a place named Vyasasthali, where by the wise Vyāsa, tormented by grief for his son, a resolve to abandon his body was made —

sanskrit: kṛto devaiś ca rājendra punar utthāpitas tadā abhigamya sthalīṃ tasya gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: — but then restored by the gods, O king of kings. Approaching that place of his, one would obtain the fruit of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: kiṃdattaṃ kūpam āsādya tilaprasthaṃ pradāya ca gaccheta paramāṃ siddhim ṛṇair muktaḥ kurūdvaha
english: Reaching the well of Kimdatta and having offered a flat sesame-cake, one would attain the highest perfection, freed from debts, O foremost of Kurus.

sanskrit: ahaś ca sudinaṃ caiva dve tīrthe ca sudurlabhe tayoḥ snātvā naravyāghra sūryalokam avāpnuyāt
english: And Ahas and Sudina — two tirthas very difficult to reach; having bathed in both of them, O tiger among men, one would attain the world of the Sun.

sanskrit: mṛgadhūmaṃ tato gacchet triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam tatra gaṅgāhrade snātvā samabhyarcya ca mānavaḥ śūlapāṇiṃ mahādevam aśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet
english: Then one should go to Mrigadhuma, renowned in all three worlds; having bathed in the lake of the Gaṅgā there and having worshipped Shulapani, the great god Mahādeva, a man would obtain the fruit of the Aśvamedha.

sanskrit: devatīrthe naraḥ snātvā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet atha vāmanakaṃ gacchet triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam
english: A man having bathed at Devatirtha would obtain the fruit of a thousand cows; then one should go to Vamanaka, renowned in all three worlds.

sanskrit: tatra viṣṇupade snātvā arcayitvā ca vāmanam sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā viṣṇulokam avāpnuyāt
english: Having bathed there at the footprint of Viṣṇu and having worshipped Vāmana, with a soul purified of all sins, one would attain the world of Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: kulaṃpune naraḥ snātvā punāti svakulaṃ naraḥ pavanasya hradaṃ gatvā marutāṃ tīrtham uttamam tatra snātvā naravyāghra vāyuloke mahīyate
english: A man having bathed at Kulampuna purifies his own lineage; going to the lake of Pavana, the excellent tirtha of the Maruts, having bathed there, O tiger among men, one is honoured in the world of Vāyu.

sanskrit: amarāṇāṃ hrade snātvā amareṣu narādhipa amarāṇāṃ prabhāvena svargaloke mahīyate
english: Having bathed in the lake of the immortals among the immortals, O lord of men, by the power of the immortals one is honoured in the heavenly world.

sanskrit: śālihotrasya rājendra śāliśūrpe yathāvidhi snātvā naravaraśreṣṭha gosahasraphalaṃ labhet
english: At the Shalisurpa of Shalihotra, O king of kings, having bathed according to rule, O foremost among the best of men, one would obtain the fruit of a thousand cows.

sanskrit: śrīkuñjaṃ ca sarasvatyāṃ tīrthaṃ bharatasattama tatra snātvā naro rājann agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
english: And Shrikunja on the Sarasvatī is a tirtha, O best of Bhāratas; a man having bathed there, O king, would obtain the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma.

sanskrit: tato naimiṣakuñjaṃ ca samāsādya kurūdvaha ṛṣayaḥ kila rājendra naimiṣeyās tapodhanāḥ tīrthayātrāṃ puraskṛtya kurukṣetraṃ gatāḥ purā
english: Then reaching Naimishakunja, O foremost of the Kurus, the sages of Naimiṣa, O king of kings, those whose wealth is austerity, with tirtha-pilgrimage as their purpose, went to Kurukṣetra in ancient times.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuñjaḥ sarasvatyāṃ kṛto bharatasattama ṛṣīṇām avakāśaḥ syād yathā tuṣṭikaro mahān
english: Then a grove on the Sarasvatī was made, O best of Bhāratas, so that it might be a great and pleasing resort for the sages.

sanskrit: tasmin kuñje naraḥ snātvā gosahasraphalaṃ labhet kanyātīrthe naraḥ snātvā agniṣṭomaphalaṃ labhet
english: A man having bathed in that grove would obtain the fruit of a thousand cows; a man having bathed at Kanyatirtha would obtain the fruit of the Agniṣṭoma.

sanskrit: tato gacchen naravyāghra brahmaṇaḥ sthānam uttamam tatra varṇāvaraḥ snātvā brāhmaṇyaṃ labhate naraḥ brāhmaṇaś ca viśuddhātmā gaccheta paramāṃ gatim
english: Then one should go, O tiger among men, to the supreme abode of Brahmā; there even a man of lower birth, having bathed, attains brahminhood; and a brahmin of pure soul would proceed to the highest state.

sanskrit: tato gacchen naraśreṣṭha somatīrtham anuttamam tatra snātvā naro rājan somalokam avāpnuyāt
english: Then one should go, O foremost of men, to the unsurpassable tirtha of Soma; a man having bathed there, O king, would attain the world of Soma.

sanskrit: saptasārasvataṃ tīrthaṃ tato gacchen narādhipa yatra maṅkaṇakaḥ siddho maharṣir lokaviśrutaḥ
english: Then one should go to the tirtha of the seven Sarasvatas, O lord of men; where Maṅkaṇaka, the perfected great sage, renowned in the world —

sanskrit: purā maṅkaṇako rājan kuśāgreṇeti naḥ śrutam kṣataḥ kila kare rājaṃs tasya śākaraso 'sravat
english: — in ancient times, O king, Maṅkaṇaka — thus we have heard — was wounded in the hand by the tip of a blade of kusha grass, O king, and vegetable juice flowed from it.

sanskrit: sa vai śākarasaṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣāviṣṭo mahātapāḥ pranṛttaḥ kila viprarṣir vismayotphullalocanaḥ
english: He, that great ascetic brahmin-sage, seeing the vegetable juice, overcome with joy, began to dance, it is said, with eyes wide open in wonder.
